tools.name: Frying pan (any size)
tools.note: A lid helps but is not required.

steps.title: Split the butter into two jobs
steps.text: Take the butter out of the fridge and cut it in two: about 10 g for the pan, about 5 g to melt on top at the end. Leave the finishing piece out so it softens while you cook.
steps.hint: Cold butter on hot toast just sits there. A softened piece melts in and soaks through.

steps.title: Melt the butter over low heat
steps.text: Set the pan over low heat and add the 10 g piece. Swirl it as it melts and stop as soon as the foam starts to settle. Don't let it brown yet.
steps.hint: High heat burns butter before the bread can toast. Low and patient is the whole technique.

steps.title: Toast the first side
steps.text: Lay the bread in the pan and slide it around once so the underside drinks the butter evenly. Toast for 2 to 3 minutes, pressing gently with the spatula, until the underside is deep golden brown.
steps.hint: Peek early by lifting a corner. The line between golden and burnt is about 30 seconds wide.

steps.title: Flip and toast the other side
steps.text: Flip the bread and toast the second side for 2 minutes more. If the pan looks dry, run a thin sliver of butter along the edge and tilt the pan so it slides underneath.

steps.title: Top with butter and serve hot
steps.text: Move the toast to a plate, set the softened butter in the middle, and let it melt in. Add the pinch of salt or a thread of honey if you like. Eat it right away, while the outside still crackles.

troubleshooting.solution: The heat was too high. Butter solids scorch fast, so stay on low and check the underside after the first minute. A dark pan hides the color of the butter, so go by smell too: nutty is fine, acrid is past it.
Too much butter in the pan, or the heat was so low the bread soaked instead of toasting. 10 g is enough for one slice, and the pan should sizzle quietly the whole time.
The slice was too thick for the heat, or straight from the freezer. Cover the pan with a lid for the first side, or give frozen bread 20 seconds in the microwave before it hits the pan.

troubleshooting.problem: It went soft after a few minutes
troubleshooting.solution: Steam trapped under the toast softened the base. Rest it against the rim of the plate so air reaches both sides, and eat it sooner. Toast does not wait.
Regular sandwich bread works with about half the time per side. Watch it closely, thin slices go from pale to burnt quickly.
